transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-02-10 10:00 PST / Duration: 60 minutes / Attendees: Elliot, Priya, Michael, Aisha, Ben, Rachel, ~120 company attendees

[00:00] Elliot: All right, good morning everyone, welcome to the Feb all hands. Thanks for joining. Uh, quick agenda: high level numbers, product updates, engineering, go-to-market, hiring, security, q&a. We'll keep it tight and then open it up.

[00:45] Priya: Quick note, I'll run through the runtime and kernel selection work up front, um, because there's a few cross-team asks.

[02:15] Elliot: First, numbers. We're at 42% quarter-over-quarter growth in API usage, which is great, but cost per token is still higher than our plan. The good news is Dedicated reservations are starting to smooth peeks in a couple of customers which helps predictability.

[04:00] Ben: On the sales side, pipeline looks healthy — three mid-market pilots moving to POC in the next 30 days. A couple of accounts looking for private deployment or VPC options, so that matches what product has been shipping.

[05:20] Aisha: For product highlights: 1. v1.2 release is targeted for late Feb — includes structured output improvements, better function-calling error handling, and the canary rollout mechanism. 2. Redwood Optimize beta will land in March for internal customers.

[07:10] Michael: Engineering: we've landed continuous batching improvements that cut avg latency 12% on our hosted pools. There's an ongoing KV cache refactor that should reduce tail latency, but it's currently behind a flag because we want more validation.

[08:40] Priya: On the kernel/compilation front — we're testing per-model kernel selection by sequence length distribution. Early runs show 8-14% perf gains on mixed-length workloads, but quantization variance is still a concern for some open models. I'll share the spreadsheet.

[10:30] Rachel: Hiring update: we're reprioritizing SRE and platform engineers; headcount freeze lifted for a few critical roles. Also rolling out a new referral bonus for engineering hires.

[12:05] Elliot: Funding and runway quick note — we closed a strategic extension in Q4 that extends runway into mid-2027 if we hit plan. That gives us room to invest in Private and compliance.

[13:30] Audience question (text chat): "Any updates on SOC 2 timeline?"

[13:45] Rachel: Security and compliance team is on a 6-week push, SOC 2 Type I evidence bundle draft due Feb 18, Type II plan scoped for Q3.

[15:00] Priya: For customers asking about on-prem options — Private has a new installer flow that reduces setup time, but networking (air-gapped setups) still requires manual ops. We're hiring a couple of infra folks to support that.

[16:30] Ben: On pricing, we're experimenting with a blended per-token + reserved throughput model for Dedicated to make enterprise procurement easier. We'll share the PR FAQ next week.

[18:00] Elliot: Quick callouts — one, keep focusing on SLOs; two, please flag any org blockers early; three, we need more cross-team docs for canary rollouts.

[19:12] Michael: There's a known issue where the KV cache refactor can increase memory on long-lived streams; mitigation is to evict prefixes earlier and we have metrics to track it.

[21:40] Aisha: Product will run a canary with 10% traffic and automatic rollback on error spikes. There's also a manual runbook for SEs to follow if customers report regressions.

[23:00] Elliot: Let's go to Q&A — please use the raised hands or chat. I'll try to answer a few live.

[24:10] Employee (Speaker 1): Hey - quick about Dedicated latency SLOs — are we committing to 200ms p95 or is that dependent per customer?

[24:25] Priya: Good question — it's per-configuration. For standard Dedicated pools our internal target is 200–250ms p95 for gen small models, but we have a sliding scale depending on model family, sequence length, and quantization. We expose performance profiles in the console.

[26:00] Employee (Speaker 2): Any concerns about competition, especially Bedrock offering managed endpoints?

[26:15] Ben: Competitors are moving fast, yes; our differentiator is cost-aware controls and predictable reserved capacity, plus the developer experience. We won a pilot this week because of our tracing and rollout story.

[28:00] Elliot: On enterprise traction — notable wins: one financial services pilot signing this quarter (confidential) and a healthcare PoC that needs strict residency. Those push Private and SOC 2 forward.

[29:30] Rachel: People note — we're introducing a manager training series in March, and a second all-hands specifically for engineering onboarding the week after next.

[31:00] Priya: A technical note: the compilation layer now has heuristics to pick kernels by median vs worst-case sequence length distribution; early switching logic helped on some batches but we still need to monitor tail behavior.

[33:45] Michael: We'll be running a 72-hour stress test on Dedicated clusters next week. Ops will share the dashboard, please don't run ad-hoc experiments during that window.

[35:00] Audience chat: "Can we get more visibility into pilot customers?"

[35:10] Ben: Yes, will share anonymized pilot list and point-of-contact spreadsheet.

[36:45] Elliot: Leadership asks: each org to list top two risks to hitting Q1 goals and mitigation plan by Friday.

[37:15] Aisha: We'll include the canary rollback thresholds and customer comms in the product runbook.

[39:00] Employee (Speaker 3): Question about open models and quantization — are we certifying specific model checkpoints?

[39:20] Priya: We curate model variants in our catalog and add Redwood-verified performance profiles; certification is on a per-model basis and we publish known quantization caveats.

[41:00] Rachel: Another HR note: new parental leave policy effective March 1 and updated reimbursement for learning allowances.

[42:30] Elliot: Quick shoutout to the infra team for the new monitoring hooks — saw multiple triages resolved faster last week.

[44:00] Priya: Will share kernel selection and perf sheets; engineering to do a knowledge share next Tuesday.

[45:30] Ben: Sales to sync with product on pilot scoping templates, we need consistent success criteria.

[46:15] Michael: Reminder: the KV cache refactor flag is gated behind a feature toggle and we plan to ramp at 5%, 25%, 50%.

[47:50] Elliot: Okay, last few q's from chat.

[50:00] Employee (Speaker 4): Any change in comp or hiring approach given runway update?

[50:20] Rachel: No comp changes today; we're prioritizing roles that unblock product delivery. We'll share updated hiring roadmap.

[52:00] Elliot: Recap: action items assigned, SOC 2 timeline, canary plan, pilot list, kernel perf sheets. Thank you team. We'll do a leadership sync mid-week to review the org risk lists.

[53:10] Elliot: Closing note — we're in a good spot but need discipline on SLOs and cross-team docs. Thanks everyone. Meeting ends.
